in the mornings: vitamin c or niacinamide paired with sunscreen

Lead
Unboxing all 15 shades of the Beauty of Joseon Tinted Mineral Day Screen — a K-beauty tinted SPF offering a wide shade range and mineral protection. This unboxing captures first impressions of packaging, shade diversity, coverage, and the sunscreen finish.

What’s in the package
- Full set: 15 individual tubes representing the brand’s complete shade lineup.
- Packaging notes: compact tubes typical of K-beauty sunscreen design, labeled with shade identifiers.

First impressions
- Shade range: Fifteen shades aim to cover multiple skin tones; seeing the full gradient at once highlights the brand’s effort toward inclusivity.
- Texture and finish: As a mineral tinted SPF, expect a physical UV filter feel with a tinted base that may provide light coverage and a matte to natural finish depending on skin type.
- Fragrance and formula cues: K-beauty sunscreens often emphasize lightweight textures; look for subtle scent and easy blending during swatches.

How to evaluate each shade (quick checklist)
- Swatch on jawline to compare to face and neck tones.
- Test in natural daylight to check true match and oxidation.
- Assess coverage: sheer tint versus buildable coverage.
- Note finish: dewy, natural, or matte and any white cast typical of mineral SPFs.
- Longevity: wear through the day to observe fading, separation, or pilling under makeup.

Who this is for
- Makeup minimalists wanting SPF with light coverage.
- Fans of K-beauty seeking tinted mineral protection.
- Anyone curious about an extensive shade range in a sunscreen product.

Takeaway
Seeing all 15 shades unboxed at once makes it easier to judge which tones will likely match a wider variety of skin colors and to anticipate how the formula performs on different skin types. For a closer match, swatch on your jawline in daylight and test wear under your usual makeup.

caption: Tinted sunscreens are one of my favorite dermatologist recommendations—especially for those with melasma, hyperpigmentation, or post-acne dark spots. The tint often comes from iron oxides, which can help provide additional protection against visible light, an important factor in pigmentation. Here are some of my favorite tinted sunscreen options: -MEDIHEAL PDRN Moisture Sun Serum Smooth & Tone-Up: pinkish tint perfect for those with skin tone similar to mine.  -Tower 28 SunnyDays Tinted SPF 30 has many shades to choose from & has skin-soothing ingredients that are great for sensitive skin. -Beauty of Joseon Tinted Mineral Fluid Sunscreen SPF 40 lightweight mineral sunscreen with natural finish. rub it in thoroughly so it’s not too shiny.  For patients with melasma or stubborn dark spots, I often recommend a tinted sunscreen with iron oxides as part of their daily routine—not just for UV protection, but also for visible light protection. Remember, the best sunscreen is the one with minimum spf30 and the one you’ll apply enough of and wear consistently every day. 🤍 #tintedsunscreen #tintedspf #sunscreenreview #drheejink

caption:
By popular demand - some of my top face sunscreens! Comment SUNNY for a DM with more of my favourites, plus my guide to using sunscreen, and common myths.

NOTE TO AUSTRALIANS - these recommendations are for the rest of the world, sorry! Check out my top sunscreens 2024 video on YT for Australian recommendations.

For reference, I have normal-to-oily skin, prone to acne and hyperpigmentation, with the beginnings of rosacea. 

All of these were either PR samples (with no expectation of review) or originally featured in sponsored posts, except Nivea which was purchased by Omar (yes the packaging is Omar approved!). This post is not sponsored.

#skincare #spf #sunscreen
transcript: (0:00) I am a massive sunscreen science nerd. Here are some of my top sunscreens. (0:04) Geek & Gorgeous Zero Feel. This is a European sunscreen. I feel like we've been waiting for this one for like 10 years and it is here and I am really impressed. (0:12) It is really lightweight and I think it is the most mattifying sunscreen I have ever tried. It keeps me unshiny for about a full half day. (0:20) No peeling issues and no eye sting for me. Just a really nice sunscreen if you're after something that mattifies oily skin. (0:26) Haruharu Wanda Airy Fit. This is one of my long time favourite Korean sunscreens. It is great for oily skin. It is mattifying. (0:32) The standout thing with this is unlike a lot of other Korean sunscreens, there is no white cast on darker skin tones. (0:38) It works really well under all the makeup I've tried it with so far. A lot of people have told me this is now their favourite sunscreen. (0:44) Nivea UV Deep Protect and Care Essence. This is Japanese. It is really lightweight and has a cooling feel when you apply it. (0:50) It does have alcohol but on my skin it didn't sting. It spreads out really nicely, super easy to get the right amount on your skin and it has a bit of a pore-filling glass skin sort of effect when you wear it on its own. (1:20) The Skin 104 has similar ingredients but somehow this is super, super light. (1:24) All of these are really lightweight, I wouldn't recommend using them if you're sweating and moving around a lot. (1:29) Look for a sunscreen that says it's designed for active situations.

caption:
Here’s how I make it-

Carrot Kanji-

Ingredients-
500g carrots (black carrots if available, or regular red/orange carrots)
1 small beetroot (optional, used for a deep ruby color if using red carrots)
2 tbsp yellow or black mustard seeds (rai), coarsely ground
1.5 liters filtered water (boiled and cooled to room temperature)
2 tsp salt or black salt (kala namak) for better digestion
1/2 tsp red chili powder or crushed black pepper
1/4 to 1/2 tsp asafoetida (hing)

Prep the vegetables: Wash, peel, and cut the carrots and beetroot into long, thick sticks (batons).
Make the spice mix: Coarsely grind the mustard seeds, salt, red chili powder, and asafoetida.
Combine in a jar: Place the vegetable sticks into a clean, sterilized glass or ceramic jar. 
Pour the ground spice mix over them.
Add water: Pour the cooled, boiled water into the jar, leaving a little headspace at the top, and stir well with a clean spoon.
Ferment: Cover the jar with a breathable muslin cloth or a loose lid. Place it in direct sunlight for 3 to 4 days, stirring the contents daily with a dry spoon.
Serve: Once the drink turns pleasantly sour and tangy, the fermentation is complete. Strain or serve cold with the pickled vegetables.

Rajsthani Chaas-

Ingredients
Curd (Dahi): 1 cup (fresh and slightly sour)
Water: 2 to 3 cups (chilled)
Roasted Cumin Powder (Jeera): 1 teaspoon
Black Salt (Kala Namak): 1/2 teaspoon
Regular Salt: To taste
Mint and Coriander: A few fresh leaves, crushed or finely chopped 

Whisk the Yogurt:Place the curd in a deep bowl or traditional clay pot (matki).Whisk or churn it well using a hand churner (madhani) until smooth.
Pour in the cold water and mix well to get a light, frothy consistency. 
Add Spices and Herbs: Mix in the roasted cumin powder, black salt, and regular salt.Add the crushed mint and fresh coriander leaves. 
Stir everything together.

caption: How to remove sunscreen stains on white shirts! I literally never wear white so this NEVER plagues me but it gets asked ALL THE TIME.
transcript: (0:00) You know those really annoying sunscreen stains that get on the collar of your white shirts that (0:04) are a pain to get out? Let me tell you how it happens and how to get rid of them. But first, (0:08) if you have white stains on your collar on colored garments from mineral sunscreens that have zinc (0:12) oxide or titanium dioxide, those should be able to come out with just regular laundering as the (0:17) stain is just the filters themselves, those white powders. Chemical sunscreens though are a different (0:21) story because the organic UV filters like avabenzone, octocrylene, and oxybenzone can bind (0:27) to iron ions in your sweat, like the sweat at the back of your neck. And so when that oxidizes, (0:32) that's what leaves that stain. What you want to do is pretreat the stain with a product that's going (0:36) to react with the iron to remove the orange. And the products that can do that are sold as (0:41) rust removal products because they're also meant to remove oxidized metals. These products are (0:46) usually powered by citric acid. Citric acid reacts with the iron to produce iron citrate. A product (0:51) that I've used in the past for this is Carbona Rustin Sweat. It has that citric acid. You want to (0:56) put it on the stain, let it sit for 15 minutes, and then wash your clothes as normal. You can also (1:00) buy pure citric acid, dissolve about three teaspoons in a cup of water, soak the stain in it, (1:06) and then wash your clothes. I've also seen people use lemon juice for this. I don't recommend it, (1:11) but you can do whatever you want. There are also some purifying rinse products like this one from (1:14) Downy that are powered by citric acid, have a low pH, and it's more for odors, but this can help. (1:19) I would consider this an add-on versus the main treatment. You just use this like fabric softener. (1:23) What I wouldn't recommend though is bleaching the stain because bleach reacts with one of the (1:28) aromatic rings in the UV filters and can turn the stain red or pink, and then it's much harder (1:33) to remove. caption: Braidy Hippo suit  Bart Bart The man who dressed up as a hippopotamus #hippopotamus #tiktokusa #truestory #braidyhippo #realstory
transcript: (0:00) I built a hippo suit, got inside it, and walked right up to a wild hippo to collect its sweat. (0:04) It was supposed to be a simple experiment, but it turned out to be the worst mistake of my life. (0:08) It all started when I was teaching kids how hippo sweat acts as a natural sunscreen to protect their skin from the sun, (0:14) and how difficult it is to collect a sample. (0:16) A young boy asked, (0:17) Why don't you just pretend to be one of them? (0:19) At first, I laughed it off, but then I realized it was actually a great idea. (0:22) So, I built a metal frame that I could fit inside, complete with a realistic female hippo head and tough, resistant rubber skin. (0:29) My team covered the entire costume in thick mud to mask any human scent. (0:33) When I finally reached the riverbank, a massive hippo was resting deep in the mud. (0:37) The second I reached out to collect a sweat sample, it roared furiously and lunged out of the mud. (0:42) Terrified, I tried to climb out of the suit, but the heavy hatch was jammed. (0:45) Worse, I started sinking fast. (0:47) I screamed for my team, but the mud was pulling me down, and the armor weighed over 150 pounds, 67 kilos. (0:54) The suit was rapidly dragging me under, and I was seconds away from suffocating or being crushed. (0:58) Fortunately, my team rushed in and dragged me out just in time. (1:01) This is based on a true story. (1:03) Search for Brady Barr hippo suit to see how it happened.

The upper lip loses sunscreen from breathing and natural moisture, sometimes within minutes of applying it. A stick formula adheres better than a lotion but any sunscreen needs to be reapplied more often there than anywhere else on your face.

caption: Ignore my week old self tan that needs to be scrubbed off 🫠 do you guys do this too?? I feel like it’s the best way to do your skincare as a morning workout person! Using the skin 1004 tea trica soothing sun milk today  #skincareroutine #morningskincare #morningskincareroutine #sunscreen #skincarehack
transcript: (0:00) This is a skincare hack for my girls that also like to work out in the morning like I do (0:03) I feel like I've seen a lot of vlogs and days in the life where girls do their whole skincare routine and then go to work out in the (0:08) Morning which everyone is different and if that works best for you, that's totally fine (0:11) Obviously, but for me personally, I feel like this is a better method because when I you know work out and I sweat (0:16) I want to wash my face afterwards (0:18) So the only skincare I use before my workout is sunscreen (0:21) That's the only thing I use get pretty sweaty (0:23) And I definitely want to wash my face when I get back from my workout (0:26) And I don't want to wash all of the skincare that I had just put on my face like an hour ago when I get back from working out (0:31) So I will literally just put on sunscreen (0:34) Of course, if you're getting up to work out like super early in the dark (0:37) You wouldn't need to put sunscreen on but otherwise make sure you're wearing your sunscreen still (0:42) Especially if you're working out outside like if you're going for a run or anything like that (0:45) Like you definitely definitely need to be wearing sunscreen and then when I get back from my workout (0:48) I will just use a tiny bit of an oil cleanser or micellar water to make sure I really dissolve on my sunscreen (0:54) And then I will cleanse my face and then do my regular morning skincare routine (0:58) Hopefully that's not like the most obvious thing in the world and like if everybody's already doing that (1:03) That's awesome (1:04) But I figured if you're putting your skincare on before your morning workout and then washing it off and then putting skincare on again (1:10) Like we could be saving a lot of product here and time, you know (1:13) So that's just how I prefer to do my morning skincare on days that I work out (1:16) Let me know if you do this too. Like is this obvious like I don't know, but I figured I would share

caption: I know everyone has their favourite time of day to work out or go to the gym, but mine has always been in the evening because it simplifies my skin care routine. I worked a 9-5 for 10 years, so I really only had time to go in the evening, and I just got used to it. But then, when I became self-employed, I kept choosing to go in the evening because it meant that I could go with the skin care and makeup I had on from the day. Sweat a lot without worrying about it, and then immediately cleanse my skin and do my evening skin care routine afterwards. And to be honest, this is STILL the best way to do it, in my opinion. However, with this heatwave, I've started going to the gym in the morning more often, and I've started to really like it. I think it takes some planning around your skin care, though, and for me that means wearing sunscreen if I know I'm not gonna sweat: - Upper body sessions - Physio - Stretching - Lighter workouts That means I can come home and not have to do anything to my face.  But if I'm going to do a sweatier session in the morning, like, for example, a leg day, I will just put moisturiser on and then head to the gym. If my gym wasn't in the basement, I would probably wear sunscreen every single time, so it does depend on your individual routine. #skincare #skincaretips #gymgirl

caption: 6 Skincare Tips I Learned From Women 🧼🧽🫧 Fellas, I thought I was washing my face the right way— until the women in my life pointed out these 6 simple mistakes. Since making these changes, I’ve had fewer breakouts, and my skin looks and feels a lot cleaner/healthier. Here are 6 skincare tips I learned from women that every man should know. What are some skincare tips that helped improve your skin? Let me know in the comments! [skincare, skincare tips, hygiene, hygiene tips, hygiene products, hygiene routine, men’s lifestyle, explore page] #hygiene #hygieneproducts #skincare #skincareroutine #fyp
transcript: (0:00) Fellas, if you want better hygiene, just watch what the women do. (0:03) Here are six skincare tips I learned from women for better skin. (0:05) One, wash your hands before touching your face. (0:08) Your hands carry oil, dirt, and bacteria. (0:10) Washing them first helps keep that off your skin and can reduce unnecessary breakouts. (0:13) Two, wash your face only using your fingertips. (0:15) Your fingertips are gentle enough to clean your skin without damaging your skin barrier. (0:19) Scrubbing with your hands or washcloth or a brush too aggressively can cause irritation. (0:22) Three, wash your neck too. (0:24) Your neck collects sweat, oil, sunscreen, and dirt just like your face. (0:27) Cleansing it is going to help keep your skin clean and your complexion looking consistent. (0:30) Four, dry your face with a clean towel. (0:32) These are going to prevent acne breakouts, protect your skin barrier, and stop bacteria buildup. (0:36) Five, wear sunscreen every single day. (0:38) UV rays are the biggest cause of premature aging, dark spots, and sun damage. (0:41) So daily SPF is going to be one of the easiest ways to keep your skin looking younger for longer. (0:45) And lastly, exfoliate two to three times a week. (0:47) Exfoliating removes dead skin cells that can clog your pores and leave your skin looking dull. (0:51) It helps your skin look smoother, brighter, and allows for other skincare products to work more effectively. (0:55) But fellas, do this during your next skincare routine. (0:57) I hope this helps.

caption:
Home Spa: How I Deep Clean My Pores

If you’d like the written step-by-step routine, comment “PORE” below and I’ll DM it to you.

A few important notes before trying this:
1. It’s easier to do this after shower, when the warmth has helped soften the buildup inside your pores.
2. I used a facial steamer to soften the buildup. If you don’t have one, you can use a warm towel as a hot compress instead.
3. Salicylic acid takes time to build tolerance. If you’ve never used it before, don’t start with a wet compress. Simply apply it to the congested areas and gently massage it in. Keep the contact time short at first, and if you feel any sharp stinging or a prickling sensation, remove it immediately.
4. Be extremely gentle when using a comedone extractor. The goal is only to remove superficial buildup—not to perform a deep extraction. Using too much pressure can damage the skin and increase the risk of inflammation, infection, or dark marks.
5. Always make sure your hands are freshly washed and your tools are thoroughly disinfected before touching your skin.

Only remove what comes out easily. Never force anything that isn’t ready.

Products used:
2% BHA Liquid Exfoliant @paulaschoice 
Madagascar Centella Watergel Sheet Ampoule Mask @skin1004official 
Hyaluronic Acid Serum @goodmolecules 
Noni Energy Ampoule @celimax.global 
Pro-Collagen Peptide Plumping Gel-Cream Moisturizer @Paula’s Choice

caption: 🚨 How to keep sunscreen from burning your eyes 👇🏼  1. Apply sunscreen at least 15 minutes prior to starting workout. 2. Don’t feel the need to completely cover your forehead in sunscreen. Your hat and glasses should cover most of your forehead. 3. Use a sweat resistant sunscreen. 4. Use a sunscreen stick so you can be precise with wear you want to apply it. 5. Mineral and zinc sunscreens tend to irritate less than a chemical sunscreen.

(0:12) The funny thing about all of this is one of my first ever viral videos was answering this exact question. (0:16) Dr. Erica mentioned it in the video, but you can wear protective clothing that acts as a sun barrier, and that's exactly what I do. (0:21) I only wear sunscreen up to about my eyeballs or my cheekbones. (0:24) I wear a good fitting hat that covers my forehead and then I also wear sunglasses which cover my eyes. (0:28) The other pro tip I have is some of that irritation in your eyes might not be from the sunscreen. (0:37) Trust me, if you get sweaty enough, that stuff will get into your eyes too and will bother it just as much. (0:41) As far as actual sunscreens go that I like, in my personal experience, I like using a mineral sunscreen. caption: Sunscreen stains are notoriously tricky, here's what actually works. Carbona's rust remover does a decent job, and here's the chemistry: some sunscreen ingredients (metals and minerals) oxidize and rust when they hit sweat or water. It's the same principle behind RustGo, the product we use as dry cleaners, just with much less aggressive acids. How to treat it: 1) Apply the rust remover, blot it in 2) Let it sit 15 minutes 3) Wash as recommended 4) Color still there? Follow with oxygen bleach and air dry inside or in the shade Honest expectations: this won't work on every sunscreen stain. There are dozens of sunscreen formulations out there, and the "why" behind a stain matters as much as the stain itself. Pool water exposure might come out clean, but the same sunscreen hit with salt water could set permanently. Another formula might only stain if you were sweating heavily. Chemistry, not consistency, decides the outcome. No two sunscreen stains are the same, but this method gives you the best shot! #SunscreenStain #StainRemoval #Laundry

caption: Hypochlorous acid spray has become one of the biggest skincare trends, but there's one thing so many people are getting wrong. It is not a cleanser. It won't remove sunscreen, makeup, sweat, oil, or dirt from your skin. Think of it as the finishing step after cleansing, not the cleansing step itself. ✨ Cleanse first with a gentle cleanser or micellar water.✨ Then spray hypochlorous acid onto clean skin.✨ Let it dry before applying the rest of your skincare. Hypochlorous acid is loved because it helps reduce acne-causing bacteria, calms visible redness, supports your skin barrier, and is gentle enough for most skin types, even sensitive skin. If you've been spraying it on after the gym instead of washing your face, remember: it's helping calm your skin, but it's not replacing a proper cleanse. Healthy skin starts with clean skin first.      #hypochlorousacid#skincarehacks#skincareroutine#skintok

Effective sunscreen should work with the skin’s biology, not against it.

transcript: (0:00) If real gold or 925 sterling silver turns your skin green, I have news for you. (0:04) One of the biggest jewelry myths is that green skin automatically means your jewelry is fake. (0:08) That's not necessarily true. (0:10) Real gold, like 14 karat gold, is 58.5% pure gold. (0:14) The remaining 40-something percent, which if you think about it, is nearly half, (0:18) is made up of alloy metals like copper, silver, and zinc. (0:20) And 10 karat gold is only 41.7% pure gold. (0:24) So it contains even more alloy metals. (0:26) And 925 sterling silver is 92.5% pure silver. (0:30) And the remaining like 7.5% are made up of other metals. (0:33) That's what the 925 stamp means. (0:34) Those extra metals are there for a reason. (0:36) Pure gold and pure silver are too soft for everyday jewelry. (0:39) So they're alloyed to make them more stronger and more durable. (0:42) So why does the whole skin turning green thing happen to some people but not others? (0:45) It usually comes down to skin chemistry. (0:48) Things like your skin's pH, sweat, humidity, sunscreen, hand sanitizer, hormones, (0:53) and even certain medications can all affect how your skin reacts to these alloy metals. (0:57) That's why you can wear the exact same ring as somebody else and have a completely different experience. (1:02) The good news is that a green mark doesn't automatically mean your jewelry is fake or poor quality. (1:06) Keeping your jewelry clean, taking it off before swimming or working out, (1:09) and letting your lotion or sunscreen fully absorb before putting your jewelry back on may help reduce the reaction. (1:14) Now if your skin is itchy, red, or irritated, that's a different conversation. (1:17) That could be a metal sensitivity or allergy. (1:19) But if it's just a green stain, don't assume your jewelry is fake. (1:22) Sometimes it's just chemistry.

caption: ☀️ Is the heat making your brow tint fade faster? Yes… but not in the way you might think…. It’s not the temperature itself that’s removing your tint. If you’ve noticed your brows aren’t lasting quite as well in summer, don’t panic—it doesn’t automatically mean your treatment wasn’t performed correctly Understanding what affects your results helps you get the most out of every appointment #browtint #hybridtint #brows #eyebrows #summer

☀️ Ireland is having a real heatwave, and while we’re all making the most of the sunshine, our skin is often paying the price.

I was delighted to join Katie Hannon and Colm Ó Mongáin on RTÉ Radio 1 to talk about some of the most common skin problems we see during hot weather. We covered much more than just sunburn, including:

☀️ Why sunburn is never “just a burn”

caption: I was scareeeed but then I wasn’t #mineralsunscreen #sunscreen #sunscreenreview
transcript: (0:00) I feel like brands are afraid to send me their mineral sunscreens now to review since I make sunscreens. (0:05) I'm very critical about the white cast, the claims, the performance. (0:08) But I really like Summer Friday's last sunscreen. (0:10) I saw they upgraded it to an SPF 50 so I went out myself and bought it at Sephora. (0:14) So let's try it out. (0:15) I tried over 700 sunscreens and today's is the new Shade Drops SPF 50 Daily Mineral Milk from Summer Friday. (0:20) This is supposed to be a lightweight broad-sppector mineral sunscreen that's SPF 50 that delivers soothing hydration. (0:25) It's weightless, skincare infused, and it's supposed to melt effortlessly into the skin to deliver a soft, natural finish. (0:30) Formulation-wise, this features a handful of antioxidant and skin protecting ingredients like ectoine, diethylhexosyringilidine, melanate, scrobilglicoside, and vitamin E, as well as allantoin and ceramides for increased skin hydration. (0:40) This formula is fragrance and alcohol free. (0:42) For that broad-spectrum SPF 50 protection, it uses zinc oxide at 5.93% and 5.46% titanium dioxide. (0:48) This formula is not water or sweat resistant. (0:50) All cards on the table, I was not optimistic about this due to it having that 5.5% titanium dioxide. (0:55) That's a mineral filter. (0:56) That is capital W white. (0:58) But as you can see, I was very gagged at how easily and quickly this melted in. (1:01) It is worth noting, I'm about a fancy 300, so I can't speak to how well this will perform on dark and deep skin tones. (1:06) But I don't think Summer Friday makes any claims about this being transparent or invisible either. (1:10) The texture of this is extremely lightweight, and while it's glowy on the skin, it isn't greasy at all. (1:14) The brand also does not make 100% mineral claims, especially since it does feature some boosters in the formula. (1:18) But unless you're sensitive to chemical sunscreens, those shouldn't be an issue. (1:21) I don't agree with the brand's natural filters claim, but everything else about the sunscreen is honestly surprisingly very stunning. (1:26) I actually like the old formula, but this is an upgrade in every way. (1:30) It sinks in quick, feels like nothing, no cast on me, great in facial hair, and good for makeup prep. (1:35) Worth noting is that this does cost $38. (1:37) So it's not a super affordable option. (1:39) If you do know a creator with a deeper skin tone who's tried this out, type them in the comments please. (1:42) But overall, I give this an 8 out of 10.

Ask a bald guy anything 🧑🏼‍🦲

One of the questions I’ve been getting the most since shaving my head is if I put sunscreen on my scalp.

The answer is yes. 

When your scalp is exposed to the sun every day, sun protection becomes a non-negotiable. I’ve been using @larocheposay Anthelios Ultra-Fluid SPF 50+ because it’s lightweight, invisible, and water and sweat resistant.

caption:
SUMMER-PROOF SKINCARE AND MAKEUP HOLY GRAILS

PR is marked with an asterisk(*).

MOISTURIZER: @sincerelyyours So Soft Cream* has the non-oily lipids to keep my skin soft and comfortable without a layer of ick on top. I mix it with a pump of @dibsbeauty Lovebeam Perfector* for light-diffusing glow without shine.

SUNSCREEN: Kose Suncut Multi Vitamin UV Essence, the zero white cast, zero grease, water- and sweat-resistant JSPF I've been devoted to since last summer, patted on with a cushion puff for the most even layer of protection.

FINISHING SPRAY: @skindinavia Makeup Finishing Spray (Matte)*. A spritz on my makeup blender before and after base and then a direct spray on face at the end seals everything down so my makeup doesn't smudge off or move all day. The Matte isn't out yet but their Oil Control version is very similar.

BROWS/EYES: The @lilybyred_global AM9 to PM9 Survival Penliner Natural in Ash Brown is amazing for me for both brows and eyes. The translucency of the liquid liner keeps it looking natural, and it does not smear, smudge, or budge for anything except a double cleanse.

BLUSH: The mousse-type Korean cream blushes are PERFECT for summer. They blur, they stay put, and they feel like velvety air. I used @hince Half Moon Cheek (in Allure Moon) today, but the lilybyred Luv Beam Cheek Mousse is great too.

LIPS: The new @heartpercent_global Dote on Mood Lineproof Lip Pencil* is super creamy, comfortable, long-wearing, and blendable enough to make a great overliner. I used shade 08 Haze Mauve and filled in with @judydoll_us Cushion Matte Lip Cream (G204 Taro Haze).

Then because I know a matte lip isn't everyone's vibe (it was barely mine until recently), I dabbed some Heart Percent Dote on Mood Over Melting Gloss* (Plum Noir) on top.

The Dibs Beauty pressed finishing powder works super well for controlling shine in my more oily areas while adding more blur effect.

This is basically the skin and makeup routine I do every day, even in hot weather or when I have plans to work out or go to yoga and know I'll be sweating. Nothing ever needs reapplication except the lip after I eat!

caption:
What to pack for a long haul flight — from a skincare consultant who learned the hard way.
Comment BAG below and I’ll DM you everything that is in mine.
I hate doing skincare mid air. It breaks me out every single time. Embarrassing? Yes. Especially when skincare is literally my job.
Airplanes are glorified tin cans recycling everyone’s air at 15% humidity — drier than most deserts. Your skin barrier is in survival mode the entire flight. That elaborate routine you see all over your feed? Your skin cannot even process it properly up there.
So my bag is not full of serums. It is full of things that deal with the actual reality of being in a metal tube for 16 hours. Hygiene first, skin survival second, landing look third.

caption: What to pack for a long haul flight — from a skincare consultant who learned the hard way. 16 items. Everything in minis. Nothing unnecessary. Hey! Here is everything that is in my flight bag for a long haul flight: HYGIENE  — Disposable toothbrush with paste  — Sachet mouthwash  — Water wipes  — Comb  — Perfume SURVIVAL  — Compression socks  — Hypochlorous acid spray  — Hydrating mist (glycerin or hyaluronic acid based — not plain water)  — Moisturiser  — Lip balm  — Eye drops  — SPF LANDING LOOK  — Tinted moisturiser  — Mascara  — Lipstick Everything in minis. Nothing full size. For the full science behind why I pack what I pack — watch the full video on my page. Airplanes are glorified tin cans recycling everyone's air at 15% humidity — drier than most deserts. Your skin barrier is in survival mode the entire flight. That elaborate routine you see all over your feed? Your skin cannot even process it properly up there. So my bag is not full of serums. It is full of things that deal with the actual reality of being in a metal tube for 16 hours. Hygiene first, skin survival second, landing look third. #flightbag #cabinskincare #travelessentials #skincareroutine #longhaulflight

4 gel moisturisers, Dermatologist breakdown:

1. Lakmé Hydra Pro: SKIP
Fragrance + menthol + multiple fragrance allergens. Too much unnecessary irritation potential for a daily moisturiser.

1. Pond’s Super Light Gel: DECENT
Glycerin + niacinamide + hyaluronic acid equals good lightweight hydration. Fragrance and limited barrier support hold it back.

1. Neutrogena Hydro Boost: GOOD
Strong hydration from glycerin + hyaluronic acid + amino acids. Fragrance is the main reason it doesn’t make my top two.

1. CeraVe HA Water Gel: TOP PICK
Fragrance-free + niacinamide + hyaluronic acid + 3 ceramides + cholesterol. Better balance of hydration and barrier support.

The lesson: Don’t buy a moisturiser because it’s viral. Read the whole formula.

Las abejas son muchísimo más importantes de lo que muchas personas creen. Gracias a ellas se polinizan miles de plantas que producen frutas, verduras y semillas que consumimos todos los días. Una sola abeja visita cientos de flores en una jornada, y toda una colonia puede llegar a visitar millones durante su vida. Además, pueden comunicarse entre ellas mediante una especie de "baile", con el que indican la dirección y la distancia hasta una fuente de alimento. caption: This is such a heartbreaking story and a lesson I think many of us need #haydenpanettiere #career #neutrogena
transcript: (0:00) Never confuse being valuable to a company with being valued by one. (0:05) I worked in HR for a decade and the Hayden Panettiere story might be the most horrific example of why. (0:10) Hayden became a Neutrogena spokesperson in 2005 and worked with them for about a decade. (0:14) Commercials, billboards, the whole thing. (0:16) If you saw Neutrogena, you saw Hayden. (0:18) In 2014, she had her daughter while still working with Neutrogena and ended up struggling with postpartum depression. (0:23) Then in 2015, she's on Live with Kelly and Michael talking about her character in the show Nashville who was struggling with postpartum. (0:29) And Hayden basically says, yes, I can relate to this in my own experience. (0:32) But then Hayden gets a call from Neutrogena saying they want to fire her for it. (0:36) Hayden's rep steps in and is like, you cannot fire her for talking about postpartum depression. (0:41) So they don't. (0:41) They just don't renew her contract for next year after 10 years of being the face of this company. (0:46) And Hayden said after that, there's nothing. (0:48) Crickets. (0:49) No one reached out. (0:50) No one said goodbye. (0:51) Thank you. (0:51) Not even a, I hope you're doing okay. (0:53) Now after her tragic passing and all of this resurfacing, Neutrogena put out a statement calling Hayden a valued, (0:59) member of their team and community. (1:01) And then they admitted that they made her feel unsupported, valued. (1:04) And that is why I will scream this until I am blue in the face. (1:08) Put yourself first. (1:09) Put your health first. (1:10) Take the sick day. (1:11) Take the leave. (1:12) Have a life outside of work. (1:13) Because you can give a company 10 years. (1:15) You can literally be the face of their organization, make them millions of dollars. (1:19) And at the end of the day, they are still a company. (1:21) And a company will choose itself every single time. (1:23) Make sure you're choosing yourself too.

caption: ✈️ Flight skincare essentials  Cabin air can leave skin tight and dry. Here are my travel friendly airplane skin essentials to choose from:  🧴 @neutrogena Norwegian Formula Hand Cream Rich moisture for dry hands. For your face, check the label and patch-test first especially if you’re sensitive or acne prone. ✨ @elizabetharden Eight Hour Cream A multi-purpose balm to seal in moisture. Apply a thin layer over moisturiser.  💦 @avene Thermal Spring Water Mist  Misty Moments that also can be massaged into the skin before your barrier cream.  🩹 @larocheposay Cicaplast Baume B5 My “nurse” for tight, irritated or sensitive skin. Apply a small amount to clean, dry areas. 👩‍⚕️@avene Cicalfate+ The “doctor” for extra-dry patches or a face that can’t get enough.  💧 @cerave Advanced Repair Balm A deeply moisturising option for very dry skin the one I packed before I lost it! Face, lips, cuticles, slugging babe.  ✈️ Simple in-flight routine: • Before boarding: Mist Moment, Apply moisturiser, then balm to dry areas. • During the flight: Reapply with clean hands when skin feels tight. • Lips and hands: Reapply after washing or whenever they feel dry. • Keep it simple: Use one balm at a time. If your skin is sensitive, avoid fragrance, harsh exfoliants, retinoids and new products while in the air. When you land you can return to normal.  • Wear SPF: Apply broad-spectrum SPF 50+ to exposed skin by the window during daylight. UVA can pass through airplane windows. That is if you’re allowed to keep the shutters open…  • Keep your mist handy for a pick me up.  • Relax and just enjoy the flight  The secret? Protect your barrier, lock in moisture and keep it simple. Save this before your next trip ✈️ Tag the friend who packs 12 outfits but forgets moisturiser 😂 #skincareroutine #traveltiktok #beautyhacks #dryskin #affordableskincareproducts  Based on clinical and life experience.

caption: La muerte de Hayden Panettiere hizo que una historia de hace más de una década volviera a salir a la luz. Una historia que involucra a Neutrogena, una relación profesional de 10 años y una conversación que Hayden decidió tener públicamente apenas unos meses antes de morir. Desde entonces, las redes sociales se han llenado de críticas hacia la marca, llamados a boicot y una conversación mucho más grande sobre lo que esperamos de las empresas que construyen su imagen alrededor del bienestar, la belleza y las mujeres. Y creo que este caso deja una pregunta incómoda: ¿qué pasa cuando los valores que una marca comunica se enfrentan a las decisiones que toma detrás de cámaras? Hayden Panettiere contó su versión en una entrevista con Jay Shetty. Hoy, después de su muerte, sus palabras están siendo escuchadas de una manera completamente diferente. caption:
Why does retinol keep wrecking your skin? Comment RETINOL for the full progression and how to know when to move up. This is not a ranking. It’s a route.

THE RULE: your skin can only use one form of vitamin A — retinoic acid. Everything else has to convert first.

Retinol needs TWO conversion steps. Retinaldehyde needs ONE. Tretinoin needs NONE, because it already is retinoic acid.

That’s why retinal is roughly 10x the strength of the same percentage of retinol, and why retinol is around 20x weaker than tretinoin. Every step up this stand is one less conversion your skin has to do.

START HERE — bottom tier

Neutrogena retinol cream. Haru Haru Wonder retinol at 0.08%, formulated alongside ceramides and bakuchiol — genuinely gentle and a sensible first bottle. Then Neutrogena or L’Oreal serum at 0.3%.

Stay here 8–12 weeks minimum. If you’re not irritated, you are not failing. You’re building tolerance, which is the entire point.

STEP UP — middle tier

The Ordinary 0.5%, Sunday Riley A+, Paula’s Choice retinol. Same molecule, more of it.

Then the encapsulated retinals. Celimax at 0.2% and Amahvas Ocean of Milk at 0.1%. Retinal is the stronger molecule, but encapsulation slows the release — stronger active, gentler delivery. Amahvas pairs its 0.1% with a 2.5% PHA blend rather than stacking harsher acids, and skips fragrance entirely. It is the best-built bridge on this stand.

TOP TIER — only if the previous step has stopped yielding results. 

The Ordinary Retinal 0.2%, unencapsulated. Nothing slowing it down.

And at the end, compounded tretinoin. No conversion, no waiting — it is retinoic acid. That is a prescription conversation with a doctor, not a shopping decision, and I’m deliberately not giving you strengths.

You don’t win at retinol by starting strong. You win by still using it in year three.

Next up in my product comparison guide series: Medicated shampoos! The best medicated shampoo is the one that controls your symptoms enough to keep your scalp clear and comfortable. But because several of these have overlapping ingredients + benefits, I thought it would help to break down which scalp types I think would enjoy them best! Remember: this doesn’t mean you can’t use or enjoy a shampoo if I recommend it for a different scalp type. Use what works best for you, always! And if you feel like you aren’t getting relief from medicated shampoos in general, definitely go see a dermatologist 💗

#abbeyyungmethod #medicatedhshampoo #shampoo #dandruff

caption: ¿Cómo logró Nubia deshacerse de su piel azul y recuperar su piel hidratada y oscura?#TikTokGrowthChallenge#theproudfamilylouderandprouder#theproudfamily#disney#fyp
transcript: (0:00) ¿Cómo logró Nubia deshacerse de su piel azul y recuperar una piel negra hidratada y radiante? (0:05) La piel con tonos azulados de las hermanas Gross y su imagen de acosadoras despiadadas (0:09) dejaron una fuerte impresión en los espectadores. (0:11) De hecho, muchas personas llegaron a pensar que su piel realmente era azul. (0:15) En realidad, ese aspecto era simplemente el resultado de una piel extremadamente seca y descamada. (0:20) En la serie, la verdad finalmente salió a la luz cuando Penny se encontró por casualidad con Nubia, la hermana mayor. (0:26) Para conseguir un nuevo empleo, Nubia cambió su nombre a Gabriel. (0:29) No solo se quitó las rastas, sino que su piel también volvió a verse hidratada y saludable. (0:33) Por eso, al principio Penny ni siquiera logró reconocerla. (0:36) Hasta que notó los restos de tono azul grisáceo en el rostro de Nubia y los folletos que llevaba en su bolso, (0:41) fue cuando comprendió de repente lo que había ocurrido. (0:44) Esto no fue un estereotipo creado por el equipo para representar a una acosadora, (0:48) sino una representación exagerada con intención artística. (0:51) Funciona con el mismo principio por el que el cabello parece más oscuro cuando está mojado y más claro cuando se seca. (0:56) Lo más interesante es que los nombres de las tres hermanas Gross están inspirados en famosas marcas de cremas hidratantes y cuidado de la piel, (1:04) lo que representa una de las mayores ironías creadas por los autores. (1:07) Nubia hace referencia a Nivea, (1:09) Gina hace referencia a Neutrogena, (1:11) Ole hace referencia a Olay.

(0:17) When Penny ran into the oldest sister, Nubia, (0:19) she had changed her name to Gabrielle for a new job. (0:22) Having taken out her locks, her skin was hydrated, (0:24) and she looked refreshed, so Penny didn't even recognize her at first. (0:27) It wasn't until she spotted the blue-gray residue on her face and flyers in her bag that it hit her. (0:31) That's because when Nubia frantically applied lotion, (0:34) her extremely dry, ashy skin instantly restored into a healthy black skin tone. (0:38) This wasn't a racist stereotype cooked up by the team to portray a bully, (0:41) but an artistic, realistic exaggeration, just like an elephant's skin. (0:45) An elephant's skin is actually dark gray, (0:47) but because it's exposed to the sun without moisture, it looks dusty and gray. (0:50) It's the same logic as hair looking darker when wet and lighter when dry. (0:53) More interestingly, the three gross sisters are all named after classic lotion and skincare brands, (0:58) which is the ultimate top-tier irony from the creators. We are back with another installment in my Abbey Yung Method Product Comparison Guide Series! This time: for scalp health shampoos. Remember: the *most* important thing is to find a shampoo that can actually deliver the benefits that you’re looking for.  So don’t be afraid to try a shampoo that I recommend for a different scalp type if it sounds like the benefits would be a good fit. This series is to help you decide between options when you’re torn between a few. Not a guide on what you can and can’t use. A lot of these shampoos will work great for many scalp types, but because a lot have overlapping benefits, I thought it would be helpful to compare how they perform & clean! Explicación clara de qué es cruelty free en maquillaje, cómo identificar productos y por qué importa. #crueltyfree #maquillaje
En esta cuenta te enseño todo sobre ese tema: cruelty free en maquillaje. Aquí encontrarás lo esencial para entender qué significa cruelty free, cómo identificar productos y por qué es relevante al comprar cosméticos.

¿Qué significa cruelty free?
Cruelty free indica que un producto cosmético no fue probado en animales en ninguna fase de su desarrollo. No es una promesa única: puede referirse a el producto final, a sus ingredientes o a la política global de la marca. Algunas etiquetas aseguran que ni la marca ni sus proveedores realizan pruebas en animales.

Cómo identificar maquillaje cruelty free
- Busca sellos y certificaciones reconocidas (organizaciones independientes suelen aparecer en el envase). 
- Lee la etiqueta: frases como “not tested on animals”, “no animal testing” o “cruelty free” son útiles, pero conviene confirmar la certificación. 
- Revisa la política de la marca en su web para comprobar compromisos con proveedores y fabricación.

Por qué importa elegir cruelty free
Comprar maquillaje cruelty free apoya prácticas que evitan la experimentación animal y promueve transparencia en la cadena de suministro. También impulsa a las marcas a buscar métodos alternativos de prueba y fórmulas responsables.

Consejos prácticos al comprar
- Prioriza marcas con certificación clara.
- Si la etiqueta no es concluyente, consulta la web de la marca o listas actualizadas de marcas cruelty free.
- Considera además ingredientes y prácticas sostenibles si buscas un enfoque más integral.

Cierre
Si te interesa el tema, sigue la cuenta para más guías sobre maquillaje cruelty free, cómo leer etiquetas y recomendaciones de marcas. ¿Tienes alguna marca en mente que quieras verificar? #crueltyfree #maquillaje

caption: Skincare Routine aufm Festival ist gar nicht so easy. Aber mit paar Drogerieprodukten geht's eurer Haut beim Camping auf Festivals deutlich besser, auch ohne fließendes Wasser: Mizellenwasser: - Inao Clean Crush Mizellenwasser - Garnier Mizellenwasser Empfindliche Haut - Bioderma Sensibio H20 Mizellenwasser Sonnenschutz: - Geek & Gorgeous Zero Feel SPF - Sun Ozon Med & Matt Sonnenfluid - Transparent Lab Lightweight Sunscreen - Riemann P20 - Neutrogena Oil Control SPF - La Roche Posay Anthelios Anti Pigmentflecken Feuchtigkeitspflege: - Isana Barriereschutz Creme - Balea NMF Base Cream Ich hoffe, mit dieser minimalistischen Hautpflege Routine aus der Drogerie kommt ihr gut durch die Festival Season ❤️ #skincareroutine #drogerieprodukte #festivals #hautpflege
transcript: (0:00) Hallo lieber Leo, ich fahre bald auf ein mehrtägiges Festival, bei dem ich nicht easy peasy morgens und abends Zugang zu Wasser habe, um mir das Gesicht zu waschen. (0:06) Falls du eine Inspo für ein Reel brauchst, Minimal Skincare Routine für Camping oder Festival wäre ein Träumchen. Dankeschön. (0:11) Ja, dann machen wir das doch mal, oder? (0:13) Festivals sind wirklich der Albtraum für eure Haut. (0:15) Aber tatsächlich könnt ihr es mit minimalstem Aufwand um ein Vielfaches besser machen. (0:18) Das erste, was ihr braucht, sind Wattepads. Da gibt es auch so kleinere Packungen, wo nur ein paar Stück drin sind, findet ihr in jeder Drogerie. (0:23) Zu den Wattepads braucht ihr ein Micellenwasser und zwar am besten eins, das man auf der Haut lassen kann. (0:26) In der Drogerie finde ich das von Inau sehr gut oder auch das von Garnier. Ansonsten ist auch das Bioderma Micellenwasser wirklich super. (0:32) Und dann natürlich ganz wichtig, Sonnenschutz. Am besten einen wasserfesten mit sehr hohem Schutz. (0:35) Gerade für Tage, an denen man viel schwitzt, finde ich den von Gigan Gortes gut oder auch den von Neutrogena, aber ich packe euch ein paar Beispiele noch in die Beschreibung. (0:41) Und ich würde euch noch eine Feuchtigkeitspflege empfehlen, zum Beispiel die Isana Barriere-Schutzcreme oder auch diese neue von Balea. (0:45) Aber zur Not kommt eure Haut auch mal zwei Tage ohne aus. (0:48) Ja, und dann wascht ihr morgens und abends vor der Routine eure Hände. (0:50) Wenn ihr irgendwo ein kleines Waschbecken mit Seife findet, am besten da. (0:52) Wenn es wirklich gar nicht anders geht, nehmt ihr ein Desinfektionstuch oder ein Wattepad mit Micellenwasser und geht damit gründlich über die Hände. (0:58) Und dann geht es auch schon an die Routine. (1:00) Abends reinigt ihr euer Gesicht mit dem Micellenwasser. Am besten macht ihr mehr als einen Gang mit mehr als einem Wattepad. (1:04) Anschließend tragt ihr die Feuchtigkeitscreme auf und morgens macht ihr Sonnenschutz drauf und tragt ihn natürlich auch regelmäßig nach. (1:09) Und das war es auch schon. Wie gesagt, es geht hier wirklich nicht um Perfektion, sondern um maximale Ergebnisse mit minimalem Aufwand. (1:14) Buttons drücken, nicht vergessen, wenn euch das geholfen hat und wir sehen uns im nächsten Video. (1:16) Bis zum nächsten Mal.

caption:
it's probably not what you'd expect...

this is my first summer in nyc so this concept of "heading out east" for the summer is completely new to me! it feels like everybody flocks from the city to the coast for almost the entire summer which in theory is fun, but it definitely adds up...

obviously if you have access to a car, a house, etc. a lot of these expenses go away but if you're starting from scratch it can be a pretty penny to get out of the city for a weekend!

i had so much fun so it was worth every penny to me but what do you think?!

#eastcoastsummer #hamptonssummer #costofnyc #nycweekendgetaway #hamptonsprices

(0:07) I will preface, everything was slightly more expensive because we didn't plan in advance and it was a holiday weekend. (0:11) But the reality is, this is probably the context you're going to be into. (0:14) First things first, we decided to rent a car, which ended up being one of the bigger expenses. (0:25) Sam and I also picked up these fire breakfast sandwiches nearby while Emily was riding. (0:28) So overall, it was a perfect pit stop. (0:30) The drive honestly ended up being incredibly painful, but we finally arrived at our Airbnb, which was obviously the biggest expense of the weekend. (0:36) You wouldn't think this from the price tag, but we honestly got a good deal because we were the first people staying at this Airbnb. (0:41) Since it was around 4 or 5 p.m. at this point, we kind of just walked around, explored the little town of Old Lime. (0:46) Somehow ended up getting drinks on the beach, which definitely wasn't the smartest use of money, but it was a beautiful night and these drinks were honestly really funny. (0:53) We also bought groceries so we could cook dinner and ended up doing a big pizza night, which was honestly so much fun. (0:58) I have no idea why the next day I woke up and decided to join Sam for a run because I literally haven't run in years. (1:03) But afterwards, we went to the cutest like coffee shop slash farmer's market. (1:07) We got coffee, breakfast sandwiches. (1:08) We also got some fresh fruit for later. (1:10) They also had chickens. (1:11) Like if you ever come to Old Lime, you should definitely come here. (1:14) This cooler that Neutrogena gave to me in PR came in very handy this weekend, but we headed down to the beach and ended up at this place called The Pavilion. (1:33) Obviously, if you don't do this, you won't have this bar tab, but it was honestly really fun. (1:37) The next morning, we basically just packed up and headed back to Long River Local on the way out. (1:48) All in, this was the total cost, which I think was worth it, but what do you think?

These are my five hacks to surviving 300+ days on the road… and exactly why I swear by each one. ✈️

For electrolytes, I use @bloomnutrition Daily Hydration or @thornehealth to stay hydrated before and during flights. 

For sleep, I pack @lemme gummies or @neurogum to make adjusting to new time zones so much easier. 

For skincare, I love the @medicube_global_official us Overnight Wrapping Mask or the @neutrogena Hydro Boost Sheet Mask because my skin always needs the extra hydration when flying. 

A good eye mask is a must, and I rotate between @slipsilkpillowcase or my budget-friendly MZOO mask to block out every bit of light. 

And for headphones, I swear by @sonyelectronics earbuds or @jlabaudio they’re under $50, the battery lasts forever, and they’re honestly better value than my AirPods… I seem to leave a pair on a plane every month, so saving $250 is worth it😂

(0:51) Ya les hice otro video explicándoles mejor. (0:53) Entonces la tecnología de encapsulación en teoría soluciona eso. (0:57) Adicionalmente no tiene niacinamida. (1:15) Entonces, si además de los beneficios del ácido acelaico, (1:18) buscas mejorar la apariencia de poros y controlar sebo, (1:21) vete por el de Skin 1004. This step can be especially important for those who take particularly hot showers and for those with chronically dry skin! 

As soon as I step out of the shower, I immediately apply a milky serum or moisturizer, which can help prevent some of the trans epidermal water loss that happens during a warm shower. 

Hot showers can aggravate inflammatory skin concerns by worsening dehydration. 

If you live in a more humid climate or have extremely oily skin, you might be more fortunate in avoiding some of the negative side effects of prolonged hot showers. 

However, I believe it’s always best practice to apply some kind of moisturizer directly after you get out of the shower.

caption: Products mentioned here: Finacea gel 15% (prescription) Dermatica 15 and 20% £20 Theramid AZID 15% £30 Dr Sam's Brightly £50 Skin1004 10% ~£15 INKEY List 10% £16 (more expensive than I remembered before I filmed, soz) Aromazone 10% £8 Now on to the ANUA azelaic acid debacle. I have made a few videos about this azelaic acid before, and I still think it's a reasonable option depending on what your expectations are. A creator called Skin Ecologic posted about how there may not actually be much azelaic acid in its free form in this particular azelaic acid because of how the azelaic acid is solubilised into the water. What this means in simple terms = there was speculation that the ANUA azelaic acid from was useless. However, other science creators have since concluded that this is not quite the case. While you can never compare the efficacy of a prescription azelaic acid to a cosmetic one, ANUA is definitely not useless BUT we cannot guarantee they'll be the most efficacious option. More testing is needed. It's a bit of a grey area. Overall, I would still recommend the watery, Korean-style azelaic acid serums for people who are just dipping their toe in the world of azelaic acid, but if you want to guarantee you'll see results you should probably go with a cream formula. transcript: (0:00) Ich gehe jetzt Skincare shoppen, denn meine Freundin hat mich gefragt, ob ich ihr eine Skincare Routine erstellen kann. (0:10) Jetzt natürlich mit Double Cleansing beginnen und da liebe ich den Hanskin Pore Cleansing Oil mit BHA. (0:16) Das ist auch das Cleansing Balm. Ich bin aber eher ein Fan von dem Cleansing Oil. (0:21) Wer mit BHA ist, ist er auch super, falls ihr auch Mitesser habt auf eurer Nase oder generell auf eurer Stirn oder Klinik. (0:27) Es entfernt auch super gut eurer Make-up, ganz besonders Wasserfest und Oscara. Very important. (0:32) Nach dem Öl-Cleanser kommt natürlich der Water-Base-Cleanser. Ihr den Pine-Cooker-Cleanser von Round Lab. (0:38) Der mit Birke ist sehr, sehr bekannt. Es haben aber sehr viele eine Birkenallergie. (0:41) Deswegen finde ich, das ist eher so ein safe pick, falls ihr ölige Aknelein in der Haut habt, da auch ganz bis zu Salicyzäure enthalten ist. (0:50) Ich habe gemeint, sie möchte keinen Toner verwenden, weil sie der Meinung ist, dass ein Toner unnötig ist. (0:54) Aber kurze Erklärung, ein Toner ist dafür da, damit euer pH-Wert neutralisiert wird und quasi preppt eure Haut auf die nächsten Produkte, die ihr verwendet. (1:02) Toner ist eigentlich immer der erste Schritt von der wirklichen Skincare-Routine. (1:06) Falls ich hier noch dazu überreden kann, würde ich ihr den von Clarice empfehlen. (1:09) Die sensible Haut ist auch unparfümiert und spendet einfach genug Feuchtigkeit, ohne dass es irgendwie ihre fundale Akne triggert. (1:16) Dann kommen wir zu den Serien, da würde ich ihr den Skin 1004 Pore-Mizing Fresh Ampure empfehlen. (1:23) Dieses Serium ist einfach dafür da, dass es eure Poren minimiert. Sharing the outdoors with my girls is my absolute favourite thing in the world 🥹, and staying sun safe means we can keep making these memories together through the summer months ☀️🥾

@CR_UK and @NIVEA_UK are sharing three easy steps to protect our skin and enjoy the sun safely:

🧢 Seek shade

👕 Cover up

🧴 Apply sunscreen regularly

I had no idea that melanoma skin cancer is actually one of the most common cancer types in the UK. By building simple sun-safe habits into our family adventures, we can help protect ourselves while still enjoying everything the outdoors has to offer. Here are a few extra tips:

🌳 Choose a hiking route with plenty of shade and some water play

🌅 If you can avoid the heat of the day, sunrise or sunset hikes can be magical in summer!

🌿 For my baby, I opt for long-sleeve layers that have a UPF rating such as Merino wool or a sun hoody.

NIVEA SUN also support Cancer Research UK’s vital research to help better prevent, detection and treat skin cancer, and have donated over £9million to date!
